subject: BlueHaven: sudden token 429s + latency spike — immediate mitigation & exec summary
messages:
From: Amit Verma <amit.verma@bluehaven.health>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: support@bluehaven.health
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 21:14:00 +0000
Subject: Sudden 429s and latency spike — production impact

Hi Chloe,

We started seeing a sharp increase in 429s and tail latency from your API around 20:40 UTC. Traffic pattern didn't change on our side — same request profile and rate. Our users are experiencing timeouts on checkout flows.

Quick facts:
- First visible spike: ~20:40 UTC
- 429 rate climbed from ~0.2% -> 8% within 10 minutes
- P50 latency increased from 120ms -> ~750ms, P95 > 2.3s

Can you confirm whether anything changed in rate/quotas or burst windows? This is impacting our SLA and we need an ETA for remediation.

Attaching a sample of request traces (bluehaven_request_samples.log).

Thanks,
Amit
Amit Verma
Head of Platform Engineering
BlueHaven Health

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Amit Verma <amit.verma@bluehaven.health>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 21:22:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s and latency spike — production impact

Amit — thanks for the alert and the logs. I'm escalating to engineering and ops now (Jordan + Neha on copy).

Immediate next steps:
- Jordan: please triage and surface root cause (rate/quotas/burst policy).
- Neha: please review any recent policy rollouts or TTL changes and recommend mitigation (temporary parameter change we can flip).

We will share an initial update within 30 minutes. We understand SLA impact and will prioritize.

— Chloe
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, Amit Verma <amit.verma@bluehaven.health>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 21:33:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s and latency spike — production impact

Amit / Chloe — quick triage notes (first-pass):

1) We see a config rollout at 20:35 UTC from the traffic-governance service that adjusted two interplay parameters: the tenant burst_window_ms (from 5000 -> 1000) and queue_headroom_pct (from 15 -> 5). That rollout targeted a different internal pool but our routing rules unintentionally included BlueHaven's tenant tag due to a recent policy alias change (alias mapping #AL-721).

2) The snapshot we pulled (attached: rate_policy_snapshot.json) shows BlueHaven's effective burst allowance dropped ~80% for 1–2s windows, which aligns with the timing and the 429 surge. The runtime then attempted aggressive request shedding which increased queuing and elevated tail latency for requests that escaped shedding.

3) Logs (excerpts):
- 2028-11-09T20:36:12Z traffic-governance rollout apply: policy alias AL-721 bound -> pool-main
- 2028-11-09T20:36:37Z route-resolver: matched tenant=bluehaven -> pool-main (was pool-isolated)
- 2028-11-09T20:37:01Z rate-limiter: tenant=bluehaven token_bucket drop=1.2/s window_ms=1000

Immediate mitigations I recommend (low risk):
- Roll back alias mapping AL-721 to previous target (restores pool-isolated routing).
- Temporarily increase burst_window_ms to 5000 for tenant=bluehaven.
- Enable emergency-fallback-route to a compatible model variant with higher concurrency for 30 minutes.

I'm attaching rate_policy_snapshot.json and a short set of request samples we pulled. I'll hold on rollback until Neha confirms approved approach for live change.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, chloe_martin@redwood.ai, Amit Verma <amit.verma@bluehaven.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 09 Nov 2028 21:46:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Sudden 429s and latency spike — production impact

Thanks Jordan — I synced with ops runbook. Proposed immediate changes (can be executed in the next 5–10 minutes):

1) Apply hotfix: increase tenant=bluehaven burst_window_ms -> 6000 and queue_headroom_pct -> 18.
2) Apply routing correction: revert AL-721 alias mapping (rollback that rollout).
3) Activate emergency-fallback-route to model-variant:redwood-medium-q4 for up to 60 minutes to absorb load while we validate.
4) Create temporary quota uplift: +25% for BlueHaven for the next 2 hours to avoid transient token bottleneck.

Risk and mitigation: small risk of increased short-term cost; low risk to other tenants because we are reverting an alias change and widening BlueHaven's window specifically. We'll run the change with a canary and monitor for 10 minutes before full flip.

I will start the hotfix unless I hear an objection within 3 minutes.

— Neha
Neha Kapoor
SRE, Traffic Governance
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 10 Nov 2028 02:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BlueHaven: sudden 429s and latency spike — production impact

Looping in leadership for visibility. Chloe — please do the following and include this summary in the customer communication:

1) Short summary (one paragraph) of root cause and immediate fix we applied.
2) ETA for full post-mortem (I want a write-up within 48 hours including why the alias mapping included bluehaven unexpectedly and what guardrails will prevent recurrence).
3) Recommendation on whether to offer a billing credit and if so what magnitude (percent of last 24h usage) — provide calc.

Neha/Jordan — do the rollback + hotfix quickly and share the timeline we followed (timestamps). Chloe — communicate to Amit as soon as we have the hotfix in place and confirm SLA implications.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Amit Verma <amit.verma@bluehaven.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 11 Nov 2028 17:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: BlueHaven: sudden 429s and latency spike — production impact

Amit — update and next steps: (TL;DR — mitigation applied, traffic stabilized)

What happened (short): a policy alias mapping deployed 20:36 UTC incorrectly routed BlueHaven into our high-sharing pool and lowered the effective burst allowance (burst_window_ms erroneously narrowed). That caused aggressive shedding for short windows and produced the 429 spike + higher tail latency.

What we did (timeline):
- 20:35 UTC: rollout AL-721 initiated (traffic-governance)
- 20:36:37 UTC: route-resolver matched tenant=bluehaven -> pool-main (unexpected)
- 20:37 UTC: increased 429s observed by BlueHaven metrics
- 20:41 UTC: Neha applied hotfix: burst_window_ms -> 6000 and queue_headroom_pct -> 18 for tenant=bluehaven (canary 1 min)
- 20:45 UTC: rollback AL-721 alias mapping started; routing restored to pool-isolated by 20:47 UTC
- 20:50 UTC: 429s returned to baseline (<0.5%) and latency P95 dropped below 300ms

Immediate customer impact: estimated affected window ~20:36–20:50 UTC (approx 14 minutes). We are recommending a 10% credit for the impacted window based on the increase in error rate and SLA impact — draft calc attached in Drive link.

Next steps:
- Full post-mortem by 2028-11-13 17:00 UTC (includes root cause, test/automation gaps, and guardrails).
- Ops/engineering will add alias-target validation and a canary gating rule to prevent cross-tenant alias leakage.
- We'll share sanitized logs and the rate_policy_snapshot.json we used to debug.

Apologies for the disruption; we're treating this as a high-priority incident. If you prefer a short call to walk the timeline, I can set aside 30 minutes.

Best,
Chloe Martin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: mitigation_playbook.md (summary), rate_policy_snapshot.json, bluehaven_request_samples.log
